assertions: The ship is lost and perished, not safe and sound
The vessel has suffered wreck or sinking at sea, its principal significator being afflicted in the 4th house, the end and grave of the matter
The ship will not return safely to port or home, and no good news of its safe arrival will come

The cargo and goods aboard, and the merchant's money and profit from the voyage, are lost with the ship, shown by Mars in his fall near the cusp of the 2nd and the Part of Fortune afflicted in the 6th disposed of by retrograde afflicted Jupiter in the 2nd

The men aboard are in mortal danger and are likely drowned or not preserved, shown by the Moon lately separating from a square of Saturn, lord of the 8th, and afterwards applying to opposition of Mercury in detriment and entering combustion
No rescue or help intervenes for the ship, the Moon being void of course after the malefic square before any benefic application
method: Classical horary astrology (Lilly, Christian Astrology Book II, ship question, whole-sign/traditional significator and Moon-application judgment)
reasoning: All testimonies are afflictive with no benefic relief: Moon separates from square of Saturn lord of 8th/9th, is void of course, then applies to Saturn and to opposition of Mercury lord of 12th/4th in detriment and entering combustion, whose dispositor Jupiter is subterranean, retrograde-afflicted and conjunct Mars; Mars is in fall near the 2nd cusp for the merchant's substance; Part of Fortune in the 6th is squared by its afflicted dispositor and the Moon; and the principal significator is afflicted in the 4th, house of the end. Together these denote loss of ship, cargo and safe return.
summary: The ship is lost and wrecked at sea, with its cargo, and will not return safely.
